requirements.text: The ESA sample(s) submitted for type approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every vehicle conforming to a type approved under this Regulation.

An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation, except that no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.

An international approval mark shall be affixed, in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form, on each vehicle conforming to the type approved under this Regulation.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN Regulation No. 10.
A vehicle shall be tested for radiated emissions for vehicle type approval.
A vehicle shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances for vehicle type approval.
The ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated emissions.
The ESA(s) shall be tested for conducted emissions.
The ESA(s) shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
The ESA(s) shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 4.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband type approval limit shall be 32 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband type approval limit shall be 32 to 43 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 2.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband type approval limit shall remain constant at 43 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband type approval limit shall be 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband type approval limit shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 3.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband type approval limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured broadband electromagnetic radiation values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the broadband type approval limits.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 5.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle narrowband type approval limit shall be 28 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle narrowband type approval limit shall be 35 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle narrowband type approval limit shall be 38 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle narrowband type approval limit shall be 45 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured narrowband electromagnetic radiation values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the narrowband type approval limit.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the vehicle representative of its type shall be tested by the method described in Annex 6.

If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the vehicle immunity field strength shall be 30 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 25 volts/m over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the vehicle immunity field strength shall be 10 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 8 volts/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-4 BCI, the vehicle immunity current shall be 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

The vehicle representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions", according to paragraph 2.1. of Annex 6, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 6.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limit shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limit shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband emission value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the ESA narrowband type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
For vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on supply lines shall be +75 V.
For vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on supply lines shall be -100 V.
For vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on supply lines shall be +150 V.
For vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on supply lines shall be -450 V.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) as described in Annex 9 at the test severity given in Table 2a in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band and at the minimum test level given in Table 2b over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
For the stripline method, the ESA shall be tested at a test level of 60 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
For the TEM cell method, the ESA shall be tested at a test level of 75 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
For the BCI method, the ESA shall be tested at a test level of 60 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

For the ALSE method, the ESA shall be tested at a test level of 30 V/m in the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 10 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

For the reverberation chamber method, the ESA shall be tested at a test level of 21 V/m in the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 7 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
For the stripline method, the ESA shall be tested at a minimum test level of 50 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
For the TEM cell method, the ESA shall be tested at a minimum test level of 62,5 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
For the BCI method, the ESA shall be tested at a minimum test level of 50 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

For the ALSE method, the ESA shall be tested at a minimum test level of 25 V/m in the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 8 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

For the reverberation chamber method, the ESA shall be tested at a minimum test level of 18 V/m in the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 6 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
During the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions".

The immunity of the ESA representative of its type to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
The ESA shall meet the starting profile test according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
The ESA shall meet the Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

For the starting profile at immunity test level II for 12 V and 24 V systems with 10 pulses, the ESA shall achieve functional status B for immunity related functions where the ESA shall be operational during engine start phases, or C for other ESA, and functional status D for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 1 at -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system) with 500 pulses, the ESA shall achieve FPSC III for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 2a at +37 V (12 V system) or +37 V (24 V system) with 500 pulses, the ESA shall achieve FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 2b at +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system) with 10 pulses, the ESA shall achieve FPSC II for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 3a at -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system) for a test duration of 1 h, the ESA shall achieve FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 3b at +75 V (12 V system) or +150 V (24 V system) for a test duration of 1 h, the ESA shall achieve FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
The starting profile requirement shall apply only to ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines which are started with a 12V/24V starter motor.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be so designed, constructed and fitted as to enable the vehicle, in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", to comply with the requirements of UN Regulation No. 10.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the vehicle representative of its type shall be tested by the method described in Annex 6.

If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, the vehicle shall withstand a field strength of 30 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 25 volts/m over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, the vehicle shall withstand a field strength of 10 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 8 volts/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6 with the ISO 11451-4 BCI method, the vehicle shall withstand a current of 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

The vehicle representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions", according to paragraph 2.2. of Annex 6, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 6.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband emission limit shall be 62 to 52 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband emission limit shall be 52 to 63 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband emission limit shall remain constant at 63 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA representative of its type on 12 / 24 V supply lines, in the configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2:2011, as described in Annex 10, for the levels given in Table 18.

For vehicles with 12 V systems, the positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by ESAs on supply lines in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid shall not exceed +75 V.

For vehicles with 12 V systems, the negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by ESAs on supply lines in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid shall not exceed -100 V.

For vehicles with 24 V systems, the positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by ESAs on supply lines in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid shall not exceed +150 V.

For vehicles with 24 V systems, the negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by ESAs on supply lines in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid shall not exceed -450 V.

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type, in the configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
The vehicle broadband radiated emissions at an antenna-vehicle separation of 10 m shall not exceed the limit E = 32 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 30-75 MHz.

The vehicle broadband radiated emissions at an antenna-vehicle separation of 10 m shall not exceed the limit E = 32 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 75-400 MHz.
The vehicle broadband radiated emissions at an antenna-vehicle separation of 10 m shall not exceed the limit E = 43 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 400-1,000 MHz.
The vehicle broadband radiated emissions at an antenna-vehicle separation of 3 m shall not exceed the limit E = 42 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 30-75 MHz.

The vehicle broadband radiated emissions at an antenna-vehicle separation of 3 m shall not exceed the limit E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 75-400 MHz.
The vehicle broadband radiated emissions at an antenna-vehicle separation of 3 m shall not exceed the limit E = 53 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 400-1,000 MHz.
The vehicle narrowband radiated emissions at an antenna-vehicle separation of 10 m shall not exceed the limit E = 28 dBµV/m, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, in the frequency range 30-230 MHz.
The vehicle narrowband radiated emissions at an antenna-vehicle separation of 10 m shall not exceed the limit E = 35 dBµV/m, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, in the frequency range 230-1,000 MHz.
The vehicle narrowband radiated emissions at an antenna-vehicle separation of 3 m shall not exceed the limit E = 38 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 30-230 MHz.
The vehicle narrowband radiated emissions at an antenna-vehicle separation of 3 m shall not exceed the limit E = 45 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 230-1,000 MHz.
The ESA broadband radiated emissions shall not exceed the limit E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 30-75 MHz.
The ESA broadband radiated emissions shall not exceed the limit E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 75-400 MHz.
The ESA broadband radiated emissions shall not exceed the limit E = 63 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 400-1,000 MHz.
The ESA narrowband radiated emissions shall not exceed the limit E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 30-75 MHz.
The ESA narrowband radiated emissions shall not exceed the limit E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 75-400 MHz.
The ESA narrowband radiated emissions shall not exceed the limit E = 53 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 400-1,000 MHz.

The vehicle broadband emissions test, intended to measure the broadband emissions generated by electrical or electronic systems fitted to the vehicle (e.g. ignition system or electric motors), shall be performed according to CISPR 12 if not otherwise stated in Annex 4.
For the broadband emissions test in configuration other than "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the engine shall be in operation according to CISPR 12.

For a vehicle with an electric propulsion motor or hybrid propulsion system, if operation according to CISPR 12 is not appropriate (e.g. in case of busses, trucks, two- and three wheel vehicles), transmission shafts, belts or chains may be disconnected to achieve the same operation condition for the propulsion.

If the operating mode defined in CISPR 12 (i.e. 40 km/h) does not activate all traction motors or auxiliary battery charging engines, the vehicle shall be operated in an alternative, steady state operating mode agreed between the Technical Service and vehicle manufacturer.

For the broadband emissions test in configuration other than "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", all vehicle equipment capable of generating broadband emissions which can be switched on permanently by the driver or passenger, e.g. wiper motors or fans, should be in operation in maximum load, excluding the horn and electric window motors.

For the broadband emissions test in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the vehicle shall be tested in the charging mode configuration (if available on vehicle) as defined in the flowchart of Figure 1 of Annex 4.
In the charging mode configuration for the broadband emissions test, in case of multiple batteries the average state of charge shall be considered.
In the charging mode configuration for the broadband emissions test, the vehicle shall be immobilized and the engine(s) (ICE and / or electrical engine) shall be OFF and in charging mode.
In the charging mode configuration for the broadband emissions test, all other equipment which can be switched ON by the driver or passengers shall be OFF.

In the charging mode configuration for the broadband emissions test, the vehicle shall be connected as shown in Figures 3a to 3h of Appendix 1 to Annex 4, depending on AC or DC power charging mode, location of charging plug and charging with or without communication.

The vehicle shall comply with the radiated emission limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS).
The vehicle's narrowband electromagnetic emissions from microprocessor-based systems or other narrowband sources shall be tested according to CISPR 12, if not otherwise stated in Annex 5.
During the narrowband emissions test, the vehicle's ignition switch shall be switched on.
During the narrowband emissions test, the vehicle's engine shall not be operating.
During the narrowband emissions test, the vehicle's electronic systems shall all be in normal operating mode with the vehicle stationary.

During the narrowband emissions test, all equipment which can be switched on permanently by the driver or passenger with internal oscillators > 9 kHz or repetitive signals should be in normal operation.

The vehicle's narrowband emissions shall comply with the limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS).

The vehicle electronic systems shall demonstrate immunity when the vehicle is subjected to electromagnetic fields according to ISO 11451-2 in an ALSE with front irradiation, for vehicles not considered as "large vehicles", at the levels defined in paragraph 6.4.2.1.

The vehicle electronic systems shall demonstrate immunity when the vehicle is subjected to electromagnetic fields according to ISO 11451-2 in an ALSE with front irradiation and with additional antenna positions, for "large vehicles", at the levels defined in paragraph 6.4.2.1.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, the vehicle speed shall not vary by more than ±10 per cent of the nominal speed of 50 km/h (respectively 25 km/h for L1, L2 vehicles).
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, in case of automatic gearbox, there shall be no change of gear ratio inducing a speed variation greater than ±10 per cent of the nominal speed.

If the vehicle is equipped with a cruise control system, the cruise control system shall maintain the required constant vehicle speed and be maintained without any deactivation during the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with the cluster operating in normal mode, there shall be no unexpected warning and no inconsistent variation of the odometer.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with the brake pedal not depressed, there shall be no unexpected activation of the brake and no unexpected activation of the stop lights.
During the vehicle immunity test, all other systems which affect the driver's control of the vehicle shall be (on) as in normal operation of the vehicle.
In the "REESS charging mode" vehicle immunity test, the vehicle shall not set in motion.
In the "REESS charging mode" vehicle immunity test, there shall be no unexpected release of the parking brake.
In the "REESS charging mode" vehicle immunity test, there shall be no loss of Parking position for automatic transmission.
The broadband electromagnetic emissions from the ESA shall be tested according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 7.
The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the broadband emission test.

Where the test is performed with a REESS, the state of charge (SOC) of the traction battery shall be kept between 20 per cent and 80 per cent of the maximum SOC during the whole frequency range measurement.
For ESA other than involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
The ESA broadband emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

The ESA broadband emissions shall comply with the limits given in paragraphs 6.5. and 7.10. of the Regulation for quasi-peak detectors, with a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 applied if peak detectors are used.
The ESA under test for narrowband electromagnetic emissions shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

The narrowband electromagnetic radiation emission limits for the ESA shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

ESAs other than those involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall comply with the requirements of any combination, at the manufacturer's discretion, of the absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5 and reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11, provided that the results cover the full frequency range of 20 to 6,000 MHz.
The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.

The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements with AM (amplitude modulation) test signal modulation, with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements with PM2 (pulse modulation type 2) test signal modulation, Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements with PM3 (pulse modulation type 3) test signal modulation, Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
The ESA absorber chamber immunity test shall use the "substitution method" to establish the test field conditions according to ISO 11452-2.
The ESA absorber chamber immunity test shall be performed with vertical polarization.
The ESA TEM cell immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3.

The ESA bulk current injection test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench using either the BCI test method with substitution method and injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA, or the BCI test method with closed loop method and injection probe positioned at 900 mm distance to the ESA, or alternatively with the ESA installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4 using the BCI test method with substitution method and injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA.
The ESA stripline immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5.
The ESA reverberation chamber immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11.
Unless otherwise specified, the ESA reverberation chamber immunity test shall be carried out using a test setup with ground plane.
The absorber chamber test for ESAs involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall be performed according to ISO 11452-2.
The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
The ESA shall limit conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply.

The ESA shall be immune to the test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The ESA shall be immune to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines, except for ESAs exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor).

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by ESAs on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 on supply lines as well as on other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

Every vehicle conforming to a vehicle type approved under UN Regulation No. 175 shall have affixed, conspicuously and in a readily accessible place specified on the approval form, an international approval mark conforming to the model described in Annex 2.

If the vehicle conforms to a vehicle type approved under one or more other Regulations annexed to the Agreement in the country which has granted approval under UN Regulation No. 175, the Regulation and approval numbers and the additional symbols shall be placed in vertical columns to the right of the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1, which need not be repeated.
The approval mark shall be clearly legible and be indelible.
The approval mark shall be placed close to or on the vehicle data plate.

The ACPE performance requirements shall be met by a vehicle with no trailer coupled, with a mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, and whose powertrain management system is properly operational.

The ACPE shall be able to limit unintended acceleration of the vehicle when an accelerator control misapplication by the driver has been detected at least when an obstacle exists in front of the vehicle when the driving direction is selected to be forward.

The ACPE shall be able to limit unintended acceleration of the vehicle when an accelerator control misapplication by the driver has been detected at least when an obstacle exists behind the vehicle when the driving direction is selected to be rearwards.

The ACPE shall regard as an accelerator control misapplication an accelerator control application having a velocity of at least 400 per cent per second over a travel distance of at least 70 per cent of the total travel distance of the accelerator control, and reaching a maximum position of the accelerator control of at least 90 per cent with that velocity.

For systems that implement force-based triggering of the ACPE, an accelerator control force greater than the triggering threshold shall be considered as accelerator control misapplication, notwithstanding the triggering conditions of paragraph 5.1.2.
For systems that implement force-based triggering of the ACPE, the triggering threshold shall be justified by the manufacturer to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority.

The ACPE shall control acceleration when the vehicle is accelerated from standstill, for a vehicle with no trailer coupled, with a mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, and whose powertrain management system is properly operational.
If the ACPE is not ready to perform an intervention 6 seconds after the initiation of the vehicle powertrain, information of this status shall be indicated to the driver.
The information to the driver that the ACPE is not ready to perform an intervention shall exist until the system has been successfully initialised.

The ACPE shall limit vehicle acceleration in order to prevent or mitigate a collision with an obstacle located between 1.0 m and 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, in the vehicle path, at the time the accelerator control is applied, provided the road is flat, horizontal and dry affording good adhesion and the weather conditions do not affect the performance of the vehicle (e.g. no storm, not below 0°C).

The ACPE shall limit vehicle acceleration to prevent or mitigate a collision with an obstacle located between 1.0 m and 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle provided the vehicle state allows for the required acceleration inhibition, e.g. the tyres are in an appropriate state and properly inflated, the brakes if intended to be used are properly operational (brake temperature, pads condition etc.), there is no severe uneven load distribution, no trailer is coupled and the mass of the motor vehicle is between maximum mass and mass in running order conditions, and the vehicle's powertrain management system is properly operational.

The ACPE shall limit vehicle acceleration to prevent or mitigate a collision with an obstacle located between 1.0 m and 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle provided there are no external influences affecting the physical sensing capabilities, i.e. the ambient illumination conditions are at least 1000 Lux with no extreme blinding of the sensors (e.g. direct blinding sunlight, highly radar-reflective environment), the target vehicle is not extreme with regard to the Radar Cross Section (RCS) or the shape/silhouette (e.g. below fifth percentile of RCS of all M1 vehicles), there are no significant weather conditions affecting the sensing capabilities (e.g. heavy rain, dense fog, snow, dirt), and there are no overhead obstructions close to the vehicle.

The ACPE shall limit vehicle acceleration to prevent or mitigate a collision with an obstacle located between 1.0 m and 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle provided the situation is unambiguous, i.e. the obstacle is stationary, unobstructed and clearly separated from other objects in the driving direction, the lateral offset between the centreline of the obstacle and the centreline of the vehicle is not more than 0.2 m, the direction of travel is straight with no curve and the vehicle is not turning at an intersection and following its lane, and the obstacle is a vehicle of category M1 or a wall like structure with a width of at least 2.0 m and a height of at least 1.0 m.

When conditions deviate from those listed for the ACPE performance requirement, the system shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy, as demonstrated by the manufacturer in accordance with Annex 3 and, if deemed justified, by testing by the Technical Service.

In the case that a collision is not prevented by the ACPE, the collision speed shall be no greater than 8 km/h higher than the vehicle speed at the point where the triggering conditions specified in paragraph 5.1.2. are met.

In the case that a collision is not prevented by the ACPE, the collision speed shall not be greater than 70% of that speed the vehicle would have had in the same position and under the same circumstances but without any ACPE intervention.

For vehicles that do not exceed 8 km/h without ACPE in the test scenarios but for which a speed reduction of 30 per cent cannot be achieved due to a low engine power to test mass ratio, the speed reduction achieved by the ACPE shall be of at least 15 per cent.

During any intervention, the vehicle acceleration shall continue to be limited by the ACPE, where the intervention may be ended only when the obstacle is no longer detected or the driver has interrupted the function.

The effectiveness of the ACPE shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields, as demonstrated by fulfilling the technical requirements and respecting the transitional provisions of the 06 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 10.
Conformity of the ACPE with the safety aspects of electronic control systems shall be shown by meeting the requirements of Annex 3.
The ACPE shall inform the driver of its intervention in accordance with paragraph 5.4.2.
The ACPE shall provide a means for the driver to interrupt its intervention.
The interruption of the ACPE intervention shall be started by any intentional action which indicates that the driver has recognised the situation.
In the case of interruption of the ACPE intervention by maintaining the accelerator control application, there shall be no rapid increase of acceleration.

The ACPE performance requirements, applying to a vehicle with no trailer coupled, with a mass between maximum mass and mass in running order and whose powertrain management system is properly operational, shall be met when verified using the test procedure described in section 6.

When a vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the ACPE, the ACPE shall be automatically reinstated at the initiation of any new engine start (or run cycle, as relevant), except when a new engine start (or run cycle, as relevant) is performed automatically, e.g. the operation of a stop/start system.
When a vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the ACPE, a deactivation warning shall be given at least at the time of deactivation.

When the vehicle is equipped with a means to automatically deactivate the ACPE, for instance in situations such as carrying a bicycle rack or towing a trailer, the automatic deactivation conditions specified for automatic deactivation shall apply as appropriate.

Where the vehicle is equipped with a means to automatically deactivate the ACPE, for instance in situations such as carrying a bicycle rack or towing a trailer, the ACPE shall be automatically reactivated as soon as the conditions that led to the automatic deactivation are not present anymore.

Where the vehicle is equipped with a means to automatically deactivate the ACPE, a deactivation warning shall be given at least at the time of deactivation unless a failure warning is given as per paragraph 5.3.3.
A failure warning shall be given to the driver when there is a failure in the ACPE that prevents the requirements of UN Regulation No. 175 being met.
The ACPE failure warning shall be as specified in paragraph 5.4.3.
There shall not be an appreciable time interval between each ACPE self-check.

There shall not be a delay in illuminating the ACPE warning signal in the case of an electrically detectable failure, except that, if the vehicle speed is greater than 10 km/h at the time a failure is detected, the warning signal may be suppressed until the next time the vehicle speed is below 10 km/h.

A failure warning shall also be given to the driver in the case of a detected non-electrical ACPE failure condition (e.g. sensor blindness or sensor misalignment) unless a deactivation warning is given as per paragraph 5.2.3.1.3.
The ACPE optical warning signals shall be visible even by daylight.
The satisfactory condition of the ACPE optical warning signals shall be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat.

Each ACPE optical warning signal, other than warning signals shown in a common space, shall be activated either when the engine start (or run, as relevant) switch is turned to the "on" (run) position or when the engine start (or run, as relevant) switch is in a position between the "on" (run) and "start" position that is designated by the manufacturer as a check position (initial system (power-on)).
The ACPE intervention warning shall be given by an optical signal.

In addition to the optical intervention warning signal, a haptic or acoustic signal shall be provided to the driver, unless such a signal is already being provided by another vehicle system comprising an object detection capability (e.g. parking distance warning).
The ACPE failure warning shall be given by a constant yellow optical signal.
It shall be possible at a Periodic Technical Inspection to confirm the correct operational status of the ACPE by a visible observation of the failure warning signal status.

Following a "power-ON" and any bulb check, the ACPE failure warning signal shall remain illuminated if any failure was present at the end of the previous engine start (or run, as relevant) cycle, unless this failure is detected to be no longer present.
Where the ACPE failure warning signal is in a common space, the common space shall be observable as functional prior to the failure warning signal status check.

The ACPE shall be provided with means, chosen by the manufacturer, to protect against simple unauthorised modification of the operation of the failure warning signal, or alternatively with a secondary means of checking the correct operational status of the ACPE.
The ACPE test shall be performed on a flat, dry, concrete or asphalt road affording good adhesion.
The ambient temperature during the ACPE test shall be between 0°C and 45°C.
The horizontal visibility range during the ACPE test shall allow the target to be observed throughout the test.
The ACPE tests shall be performed when there is no wind liable to affect the results.

Where tests are conducted, at the request of the manufacturer and with the agreement of the Technical Service, under deviating test conditions (suboptimal conditions, e.g. on a not dry surface or below the specified minimum ambient temperature), the system shall still meet the performance requirements.
The vehicle shall meet the ACPE test requirements at the minimum mass (mass in running order with an additional mass of maximum 125 kg).

The vehicle shall meet the ACPE test requirements at any other mass up to the technically permissible maximum laden mass as defined by the manufacturer, where the technical service deems testing at such a mass justified.
The ACPE shall meet the accelerator control misapplication test with a lateral offset between the centreline of the target and the centreline of the vehicle of between 0.0 m and 0.2 m.

The ACPE shall meet the accelerator control misapplication test performed with and without an expected ACPE intervention, both in a forward and rearward direction, at least with the vehicle situated 1.0 m (+0.1 m tolerance) and 1.5 m (-0.1 m tolerance) from the target position at the start of the test as detailed in Table 1.

The ACPE shall meet the forward accelerator control misapplication test with the target present (with ACPE intervention) at a distance to target of 1.0 m (+0.1 m tolerance) with a lateral offset tolerance of +/-0.2 m.

The ACPE shall meet the forward accelerator control misapplication test without the target (without ACPE intervention or with ACPE deactivated) at a distance to speed measuring point of 1.0 m (+0.1 m tolerance).

The ACPE shall meet the forward accelerator control misapplication test with the target present (with ACPE intervention) at a distance to target of 1.5 m (-0.1 m tolerance) with a lateral offset tolerance of +/-0.2 m.

The ACPE shall meet the forward accelerator control misapplication test without the target (without ACPE intervention or with ACPE deactivated) at a distance to speed measuring point of 1.5 m (-0.1 m tolerance).

The ACPE shall meet the rearward accelerator control misapplication test with the target present (with ACPE intervention) at a distance to target of 1.0 m (+0.1 m tolerance) with a lateral offset tolerance of +/-0.2 m.

The ACPE shall meet the rearward accelerator control misapplication test without the target (without ACPE intervention or with ACPE deactivated) at a distance to speed measuring point of 1.0 m (+0.1 m tolerance).

The ACPE shall meet the rearward accelerator control misapplication test with the target present (with ACPE intervention) at a distance to target of 1.5 m (-0.1 m tolerance) with a lateral offset tolerance of +/-0.2 m.

The ACPE shall meet the rearward accelerator control misapplication test without the target (without ACPE intervention or with ACPE deactivated) at a distance to speed measuring point of 1.5 m (-0.1 m tolerance).

The ACPE shall meet the accelerator control misapplication test when, from stationary with the corresponding driving direction selected and the steering control maintained in the neutral position, the accelerator control is operated to achieve the triggering conditions of paragraph 5.1.2. before the vehicle reaches a speed of 0.5 km/h.
The approval mark affixed to a vehicle approved with regard to the ACPE shall follow the arrangement shown in Annex 2 with the dimension a of 8 mm min.

The special requirements for documentation, fault strategy and verification of Annex 3 shall also apply to safety related functions identified in this Regulation which are controlled by electronic system(s).

The information disclosed for type approval shall show that "The System" respects, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified elsewhere in this Regulation.
The information disclosed for type approval shall show that "The System" is designed to operate in such a way that it does not induce safety critical risks.

The manufacturer shall provide a documentation package which gives access to the basic design of "The System" and the means by which it is linked to other vehicle systems or by which it directly controls output variables.
The documentation shall explain the function(s) of "The System" and the safety concept, as laid down by the manufacturer.
The documentation shall be brief, yet provide evidence that the design and development has had the benefit of expertise from all the system fields which are involved.
For periodic technical inspections, the documentation shall describe how the current operational status of "The System" can be checked.
"The System" shall be designed to operate, under non-fault and fault conditions, in such a way that it does not induce safety critical risks.
"The System" shall respect, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified elsewhere in this Regulation.
"The System" shall be developed according to the development process/method declared by the manufacturer.

The formal documentation package for the approval, containing the material listed in paragraph 3. (with the exception of that of paragraph 3.4.4.), shall be supplied to the Technical Service at the time of submission of the type approval application.

The additional material and analysis data of paragraph 3.4.4. shall be retained by the manufacturer but made open for inspection at the time of type approval, and shall remain available for a period of 10 years counted from the time when production of the vehicle is definitely discontinued.

A description shall be provided which gives a simple explanation of all the control functions of "The System" and the methods employed to achieve the objectives, including a statement of the mechanism(s) by which control is exercised.
Any described function of "The System" that can be over-ridden shall be identified and a further description of the changed rationale of the function's operation provided.
A list of all input and sensed variables of "The System" shall be provided and the working range of these defined.
A list of all output variables which are controlled by "The System" shall be provided, with an indication given, in each case, of whether the control is direct or via another vehicle system.
The range of control (paragraph 2.8.) exercised by "The System" on each controlled output variable shall be defined.
Limits defining the boundaries of functional operation (paragraph 2.9.) of "The System" shall be stated where appropriate to system performance.
A list shall be provided collating all the units of "The System" and mentioning the other vehicle systems which are needed to achieve the control function in question.
An outline schematic showing the units of "The System" in combination shall be provided with both the equipment distribution and the interconnections made clear.

Each unit of "The System" shall be clearly and unambiguously identifiable (e.g. by marking for hardware and marking or software output for software content) to provide corresponding hardware and documentation association.

Where functions of "The System" are combined within a single unit or within a single computer but shown in multiple blocks in the block diagram, only a single hardware identification marking shall be used.

The identification of a unit of "The System" shall define the hardware and software version and shall be changed where the software changes such as to alter the function of the unit as far as this Regulation is concerned.
In case of a failure of "The System", the driver shall be warned, for example by warning signal or message display.

When "The System" is not deactivated by the driver, e.g. by turning the ignition (run) switch to "off" or by switching off that particular function if a special switch is provided for that purpose, the failure warning shall be present as long as the fault condition persists.

If the chosen provision for safe operation under fault conditions selects a partial performance mode of operation under certain fault conditions, then these conditions shall be stated and the resulting limits of effectiveness of "The System" defined.

If the chosen provision for safe operation under fault conditions selects a second (back-up) means to realise the vehicle control system objective, the principles of the change-over mechanism, the logic and level of redundancy and any built in back-up checking features shall be explained and the resulting limits of back-up effectiveness defined.

If the chosen provision for safe operation under fault conditions selects the removal of the Higher Level Function, all the corresponding output control signals associated with this function shall be inhibited, and in such a manner as to limit the transition disturbance.

The documentation of "The System" shall be supported by an analysis which shows, in overall terms, how the system will behave on the occurrence of any individual hazard or fault which will have a bearing on vehicle control performance or safety.
The chosen analytical approach(es) shall be established and maintained by the Manufacturer and shall be made open for inspection by the Technical Service at the time of the type approval.
The safety approach at the concept (vehicle) level shall include consideration of interactions with other vehicle systems and shall be based on a Hazard / Risk analysis appropriate to system safety.
The safety approach at the system level shall be based on a Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA), a Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) or any similar process appropriate to system safety.

The validation of "The System" shall use, for example, Hardware in the Loop (HIL) testing, vehicle on-road operational testing, or any means appropriate for validation, and the validation plans shall be suitable and have been completed.
The safety concept documentation shall itemize the parameters being monitored.

The safety concept documentation shall set out, for each fault condition which will have a bearing on vehicle control performance or safety, the warning signal to be given to the driver and/or to service/technical inspection personnel.

The safety concept documentation shall describe the measures in place to ensure "The System" does not prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle when the performance of "The System" is affected by environmental conditions e.g. climatic, temperature, dust ingress, water ingress, ice packing.
"The System" shall perform the functions declared by the manufacturer under non-fault conditions, including, for complex electronic systems, scenarios whereby a declared function is overridden.

The results of verifying the reaction of "The System" to simulated failures of individual units shall correspond with the documented summary of the failure analysis, to a level of overall effect such that the safety concept and execution are confirmed as being adequate.
